card: Bitcoin Core gains descriptor inspection and multisig safety analysis via AnalyzeDescriptor, adding a verbose option to getdescriptorinfo and a new analyzedescriptor wallet RPC. Currently, participants joining a multisig wallet cannot use Core to verify whether a coordinator-supplied descriptor strictly enforces the agreed k-of-n rules without trapdoors like duplicate cosigners or unexpected spend paths. The new methods inspect descriptor policies and key inventories, while the wallet RPC reports key ownership, signing capabilities, and address derivation even when locked. This work depends on PR 35918 and forms part of the multisig setup workflow tracked in issue 35645.
evidence: PR description: "Before importing a multisig descriptor received from a coordinator, each participant needs to check that it is the setup they agreed on: a k-of-n where any k cosigners can spend and nothing else can, that their own key is in it, and that they all derived the same first address. Today nothing in Core reports what a descriptor commits to, so tools had to parse the descriptor string by hand, as the multisig wizard in #36325 (now closed) did."

Commit e14990c876: "Two cosigner slots are the same holder if they share a root key, or derive the same key at the first address (an xpub and its own child). Core accepts such descriptors, and fewer signers than the threshold can spend from them."
problem: When joining a multisig setup, participants must verify that a coordinator-supplied descriptor adheres strictly to their agreed k-of-n policy, contains their key, and generates identical addresses. Core currently does not report what spending policies a descriptor commits to, requiring external tools to parse descriptor strings manually and risking vulnerabilities like repeated keys that lower effective signing thresholds.

risk.why: Bugs in descriptor policy inspection or key matching could cause users or multisig coordination tools to misjudge whether a descriptor is safe to fund or sign.

scope_notes: Large multi-layered change spanning script descriptors, RPC helpers, and wallet interfaces (+3408/-104). The first 3 commits are shared from PR #35918, and commits 4 through 7 adapt descriptor inspection code from w0xlt with minor modifications listed in the description. Includes substantial unit, functional, and fuzz test additions.
summary: Adds structural descriptor inspection and multisig safety analysis to Bitcoin Core, exposed via a new `analyzedescriptor` wallet RPC and a `verbose` flag on `getdescriptorinfo`. Core reconstructs key inventories and policy trees to verify whether an output descriptor matches a recognized k-of-n multisig configuration without hidden spend paths or duplicate cosigner keys. The wallet RPC correlates descriptor keys with the loaded wallet to determine cosigner ownership, reports whether the wallet can sign, and computes the first receive address.
